name: Corn chamomile
grown_as: A wild annual of arable fields, sown from a wild-flower packet in William's upper orchard, 20 to 50 cm.
habit: A branched annual 20 to 50 cm, sprawling at the base and then upright, greyish and softly downy, with only a faint smell.

leaf.type: Simple but deeply divided once or twice (pinnately) into short, narrow, flat lobes
leaf.outline: Oblong overall, 2 to 5 cm; lobes 1 to 2 mm wide, short and flat (not hair-thin), each ending in a tiny bristle point
leaf.tip: Lobes with a tiny bristle point

flower.form: A small single daisy whose centre becomes domed with age
flower.petals: About 12 to 20 white ray florets, oblong with a small notched tip
flower.centre: A yellow disc, flat at first then rising into a low cone; between the florets are tiny pointed scales (seen if the head is pulled apart)
flower.behind: Downy green bracts with pale papery edges
flower.carried: Alone at the tips of long branch stalks that thicken a little under the head, facing up

fruit: Rays wither; the disc forms a brownish-yellow cone. Seeds tiny, straw-brown, four-angled and ribbed, with a small raised rim at the top and no fluff.
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves. The first true leaves are already cut into a few narrow lobes and are downy.
winter: Nothing, or small self-sown seedlings that sometimes overwinter.

leaf: leaf divided once or twice into short narrow flat lobes, not hair-thin
bloom: bracts behind with pale papery edges
flower: many small white daisies, one on each branch tip

look_alikes: Scentless mayweed has hairless, hair-thin leaf segments, a solid domed disc without scales and is more often seen. Scented mayweed (German chamomile) has a hollow cone, rays that turn down and a sweet smell. Stinking chamomile smells foul and has nearly hairless leaves. Chamomile (Chamaemelum nobile) is a low perennial mat smelling of apples.
